title: Exact-Width Words and Bounded Ranks
statement: For every $w\in\mathbb{N}$ and every predicate $p$ on binary words, there exists a word $u$ of length $w$ satisfying $p$ if and only if there exists $i\in\mathbb{N}$ with $i<2^w$ such that the width-$w$ little-endian binary word of $i$ satisfies $p$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a predicate on binary words
replaced:
For every width $w$ and every predicate $p$ on boolean words: there exists a word
$u$ with $|u| = w$ satisfying $p$ if and only if there exists a rank $i < 2^w$ such
that $p$ holds of the width-$w$ binary word of $i$.
